subject: Follow-up: EuroHealthTech region preference & VPC option discussion
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>
To: Martin Vogel <m.vogel@eurohealthtech.com>, Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@eurohealthtech.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 10:12:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call recap & quick clarification on residency needs

Hi Martin / Elena,

Thanks again for the time today — good conversation and appreciate the clarity on the workloads you plan to run (clinical summarization + patient-intake routing). A couple quick notes and an ask so we can prioritize the right hosting path: 

- Residency constraint you mentioned: keep all patient-identifiable data and inference logs inside the EU (preferably Germany / Frankfurt region).
- Throughput expectation: bursty daytime traffic for onboarding waves, sustained low qps at night.
- Security posture: SOC 2 + customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) needed for production.

To confirm our next steps and avoid back-and-forth, can you confirm whether EuroHealthTech requires: 
1) A private VPC (customer-managed networking) or on-prem appliance?
2) Whether a hosted EU-only API with a contractual data boundary would be sufficient (we can serve from FRA region and restrict cross-region fallback), or
3) Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pool) in Frankfurt where you control keys and we provide network peering?

I'll map each option to expected lead time, pricing delta, and what we can guarantee for cross-region routing/fallback. Attaching the short security checklist you asked for and a one-page diagram of the three deployment paths.

Proposed next call: Thu 26 Nov, 09:00 CET (45 mins) — confirm if that works and who from your infra team should join.

Thanks,
Stephanie Nguyen
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference

Attachments: EuroHealthTech_Security_Checklist.pdf, proposed_execution_diagram.png
From: Martin Vogel <m.vogel@eurohealthtech.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@eurohealthtech.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 09:38:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & quick clarification on residency needs

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks for the clear recap. To answer directly:
- We need production inference for identifiable patient data to remain physically in the EU, and we prefer DE-FRA as primary.
- A hosted EU-only API is acceptable only if: 
  * Processing and logs remain in DE (no automatic cross-region failover that moves identifiable payloads), and
  * We can have customer-managed keys (bring-your-own-KMS) or HSM-backed encryption for sensitive artifacts.
- Dedicated capacity in FRA looks attractive if it shortens lead time compared to a full private VPC.
- On-prem is a last resort due to maintenance overhead.

One important constraint: our privacy team requires a contractual guarantee that, under normal fallback behavior, token-level inference will not be routed outside the EU. We can accept an automated fallback to a sibling EU region (e.g., NL-AMS) but not to APAC or US.

We'll try to have our lead cloud engineer, Elena, join the call on Thursday.

Regards,
Martin
Head of Platform Engineering
EuroHealthTech
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>
To: Martin Vogel <m.vogel@eurohealthtech.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 26 Nov 2026 08:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & quick clarification on residency needs

Martin — really helpful, thanks. Quick alignment from our side before Thursday's call so Elena has details to review with infra: 

Option A — Hosted (EU only):
- We can serve from DE-FRA with our hosted control plane.
- Data plane (inference, logs) can be constrained to EU regions by contract and routing policy.
- BYOK via KMS integration is supported for stored artifacts; for runtime inference keys we offer HSM-backed key wrapping on Dedicated/Private only.
- Cross-region fallback: policy-based; default policy can restrict fallbacks to EU-only regions (FRA, AMS). We cannot guarantee zero-everywhere fallback for multi-region outages, but we will provide SLA language limiting fallback destinations to EU unless explicitly authorized.
- Lead time: immediate (days) to get a test endpoint; production with contractual guarantees ~2–3 weeks for control-plane entitlements and KMS setup.

Option B — Dedicated capacity (Reserved in FRA):
- Provisioned GPU pool in FRA, isolated tenant, supports HSM key wrapping and peering with your VPC.
- Full control over routing and stronger isolation; fallback stays in the same dedicated cluster class (we can disable cross-region failover).
- Lead time: 4–6 weeks for capacity provisioning and networking setup.

Option C — Private VPC / On-prem appliance:
- We can deploy a private control plane with customer-managed networking or an on-prem bundle.
- Longest lead time (6–12+ weeks) and requires joint runbook for upgrades.

Notes on prefix caching and cost tradeoffs: Hosted will still let you use KV/prefix caching to reduce token cost, but deterministic placement of caches is easier on Dedicated/Private. If you need strict data locality for cached prefixes, Dedicated is recommended.

Action items for Thursday:
- We will prepare a redlined sample contract clause that limits cross-region fallback to EU-only and outlines KMS/HSM options.
- Laura will prepare an annotated diagram showing where logs and caches live in each option.

Call confirmed: Thu 26 Nov, 09:00 CET — joining: Martin, Elena, Stephanie, Marcus, Laura.

Thanks,
Stephanie

Hi all,

Thanks for the pre-call notes, that helped. A couple clarifications from our infra side after reviewing the checklist: 

- For BYOK we need end-to-end control of key lifecycle (rotation policies, audit logs). Will Redwood provide KMS audit events to our SIEM?
- For fallback: policy that restricts fallback to "EU regions only" is acceptable. We will still require a notification window and an emergency escalation path if fallback to non-EU is required (e.g., large-scale outage).
- Can you confirm whether Dedicated in FRA will allow private peering (no public ingress) and support HSM key wrapping at rest and in transit?

If those are yes, we are comfortable moving forward with a Dedicated evaluation in FRA — we'd like a 4-week pilot with test data and a small reserved pool. Please send a short SOW and a draft pilot order so procurement can review.

Elena Rossi
Lead Cloud Engineer
EuroHealthTech
